thread:
deploy-bot: Canary deploy for sdk@3.9.0 started on canary host canary-12
maria: seeing spike in streaming errors in canary metrics :rotating_light:
sam: link to grafana: <https://grafana.rw/incoming/d/streams/canary?var=canary-12>
sam: errors are mostly 400/422 handshake/frame decode
lucas: logs (filtered):
```json
{"ts":"2026-03-14T12:04:22Z","service":"stream-proxy","msg":"handshake failed","err":"unknown header x-rw-stream-proto v2"}
```
erica: wait, v3.9 changed header name from `x-rw-stream-proto` -> `x-rw-stream` for the new client framing
oncall-nyc: are production clients compatible? what's % impacted?
support-bot: 30min window summary: 12 customers with streaming sessions, 18% of sessions experienced disconnects, 4 support tickets opened
maria: canary traffic is low but this will affect older clients, paging subscribers might see cursor resets
jack: starting incident channel, tagging oncall and SRE
ops-bot: /incident create "sdk streaming header mismatch" severity P2
oncall-nyc: I'll take this. quick customer impact check: list of customers with active streaming: acct-123, acct-456, acct-omega
sam: reproducer locally: run client v3.8 -> server v3.9 and you see handshake rejected
lucas: root cause: server expects new header name, treats unknown header version as fatal; older clients still sending old header -> immediate disconnect
erica: rolling change should have been backward-compatible. need hotfix or fallback
maria: mitigation options:
- add compatibility fallback in proxy to accept both headers (fast)
- toggle feature flag to disable streaming framing changes (kill-switch)
- rollback canary (safe but slower)
oncall-nyc: do we have a kill flag? name?
sam: feature flag is `sdk_stream_frame_compat` but default was ON for release — looks like the new behavior requires it OFF to accept old header; docs mixed up
ops-bot: ff status: `sdk_stream_frame_compat=true` across prod and canary
lucas: we should toggle to `false` to re-enable compatibility handling in the proxy
erica: who can flip that now? need fast path, don't want to deploy code
jack: i can toggle via admin console, but need approval from oncall
oncall-nyc: approved, please flip and monitor
maria: toggle command (console):
```bash
redwood-ffctl set sdk_stream_frame_compat false --env canary,prod --author jack
```
maria: done for canary, rolling to prod now
support-bot: alert: rollback flag change propagated to canary in 12s
sam: canary metrics normalizing, handshake errors down to ~1%
oncall-nyc: proceed to disable across prod
jack: running for prod now, command output: `success: sdk_stream_frame_compat=false on 12/12 hosts`
maria: monitoring... graphs look stable, no new disconnects
support-bot: customer tickets paused. support to confirm with affected accounts
erica: next steps: block the release (stop rollout), we should not continue 3.9 until compatibility patch lands
lucas: initiating immediate rollback for the release group
ops-bot: /deploy rollback release/2026-03-14-3.9 --canary --reason "header compat break"
ops-bot: rollback queued, rolling back canary -> previous stable
sam: rollback complete on canary, starting prod rollback in 90s
maria: heads-up to customers: sending proactive notice to streaming customers that we had a partial outage and mitigated with flag toggle; full rollback will follow
support-bot: draft message:
"We're investigating intermittent streaming disconnects affecting some clients after a recent SDK/server update. We applied a compatibility flag to restore service and are rolling back the release while we prepare a proper fix. No data loss expected."
erica: looks good, send now
jack: message sent to affected accounts, support assigned followups
oncall-nyc: will coordinate postmortem and next steps: fix options:
- make proxy accept both header names by default and log deprecated header
- add integration tests covering client-server combos
- adjust rollout docs and FF default
maria: create incident ticket in JIRA `INC-5821` and assign to eng-runtime
ops-bot: /incident update INC-5821 status: mitigated details: `ff toggled false`, `rollback started`
sam: timeline notes:
- 12:03 deploy canary started
- 12:05 handshake errors spike
- 12:10 ff toggled for canary
- 12:16 ff rolled to prod
- 12:20 rollback initiated
- 12:25 rollback complete on canary
lucas: assigning patch to me, will prepare compatibility handler + tests, aim for patch release tomorrow
erica: thanks everyone. please add any logs/links to the incident ticket. postmortem scheduled for 24h
oncall-nyc: closing this thread for live mitigation. reopen if regressions appear :thumbsup:
